category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: An Approved Mental Health Professional (AMHP) arrives on the ward at 9pm with section papers for a new admission.
question: Under the trust's Receipt and Scrutiny policy, which staff are authorised to receive and accept section papers on behalf of the Hospital Managers?
options: Any registered nurse or health care assistant on duty
Qualified nursing staff at Band 5 and above
Only the ward manager or matron
Only a Mental Health Act (MHA) Administrator
rationale: The trust delegates receipt of section papers to qualified nursing staff Band 5 and above, all of whom must have had specific training on receiving and accepting MHA paperwork.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Receipt, Scrutiny and Management of Section Papers Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: December 2024, issue 04, review December 2027 (minor amendment June 2025)

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
question: Once a Band 5 nurse has established that section papers for a Section 3 admission are legal, which form do they complete to formally accept the papers on behalf of the Hospital Managers?
options: Form H3
Form H1
Form H4
Form A11
rationale: The trust policy directs that Form H3 is completed for sections 2, 3 and 4 once the legality of the papers has been established.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Receipt, Scrutiny and Management of Section Papers Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: December 2024, issue 04, review December 2027 (minor amendment June 2025)

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: An informal patient on the ward has been placed under a doctor's holding power and the paperwork has just been handed to the nurse in charge.
question: Which form does the trust policy say the receiving nurse completes to accept papers for a Section 5(2)?
options: Form H3 in full
Part 1 of Form H4
Part 2 of Form H1
Form A11
rationale: The policy lists Part 2 of Form H1 as the acceptance record for Section 5(2), separate from Form H3 which covers sections 2, 3 and 4.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Receipt, Scrutiny and Management of Section Papers Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: December 2024, issue 04, review December 2027 (minor amendment June 2025)

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
question: Mental Health Act (MHA) Administrators in this trust are based on how many sites, and where?
options: One central site at Kingsway House, Kingsway Hospital, Derby
One administrator is based on each inpatient ward
Three sites, one for each division of the trust
Two sites: the Derwent Unit, Royal Hospital, Chesterfield and Kingsway House, Kingsway Hospital, Derby
rationale: The policy names two MHA administration bases: the Derwent Unit at the Royal Hospital in Chesterfield, and Kingsway House at Kingsway Hospital in Derby.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Receipt, Scrutiny and Management of Section Papers Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: December 2024, issue 04, review December 2027 (minor amendment June 2025)

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: You are checking the papers for a Section 2 admission and notice the two medical examinations were seven days apart.
question: According to the trust's list of errors, how should this be treated?
options: It is a rectifiable error and can be corrected within 14 days
It is acceptable because the examinations were within 14 days of the application
It cannot be rectified and would render the detention invalid
It only matters for Section 3, not Section 2
rationale: The trust policy lists medical examinations more than 5 clear days apart (sections 2 and 3) among the errors which cannot be rectified and which render the detention invalid.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Receipt, Scrutiny and Management of Section Papers Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: December 2024, issue 04, review December 2027 (minor amendment June 2025)

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: The patient's surname is spelled two different ways across the application and the medical recommendations.
question: How does the trust policy classify this error?
options: Rectifiable by the author within 14 days of the patient being admitted on a section
Fundamental, so a fresh application must be made immediately
Rectifiable, but only by the Mental Health Act (MHA) office, not the author
Not an error at all, as Section 6(3) allows staff to act without further proof
rationale: The policy lists a patient's name and address not being fully completed, inaccurate or not identical on all forms among the errors rectifiable under Section 15 within 14 days of admission.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Receipt, Scrutiny and Management of Section Papers Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: December 2024, issue 04, review December 2027 (minor amendment June 2025)

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A nurse establishes that a newly admitted patient's detention papers are invalid.
question: Which set of actions does the trust policy require of nursing staff?
options: Wait until the Mental Health Act (MHA) office opens the next working day before telling anyone

Notify the Responsible Clinician or Approved Clinician, the Approved Mental Health Professional (AMHP) and the MHA office, tell the patient they are no longer detained, and consider whether Section 5(4) or 5(2) is needed
Notify only the Responsible Clinician and continue to treat the patient as detained until the papers are corrected
Ask the applicant to complete fresh papers and say nothing to the patient until they arrive
rationale: The policy sets out that nursing staff notify the Responsible Clinician or Approved Clinician, the AMHP and the MHA office, inform the patient they are no longer detained and of their right to legal advice, and give consideration to the use of Section 5(4) or 5(2).
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Receipt, Scrutiny and Management of Section Papers Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: December 2024, issue 04, review December 2027 (minor amendment June 2025)

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A patient is admitted on a Hospital Order made by the court and there is an obvious error on the paperwork.
question: What does the trust policy say should happen?
options: The error is rectified under Section 15 within 14 days like any other section paper
The nurse in charge should refuse to accept the patient until the court reissues the order
The Responsible Clinician should correct the paperwork and countersign the change
The Mental Health Act (MHA) office should discuss the error with the Clerk of the Court, and should not invalidate the section unless the court directs it
rationale: Section 15 rectification does not apply to Hospital Orders or other court documents, and the trust policy directs the MHA office to raise serious errors with the Clerk of the Court rather than invalidate the section.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Receipt, Scrutiny and Management of Section Papers Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: December 2024, issue 04, review December 2027 (minor amendment June 2025)

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
question: Under the trust's protocol for retention and storage of section papers, how long are hard copies kept once scanned, and what must happen before they are destroyed?
options: A maximum of 28 days, and a second check must be completed by a different member of the team before the papers are cross shredded
A maximum of 7 days, after which the ward manager signs them off for shredding
Six months, held in the ward's locked Mental Health Act (MHA) file
They are kept indefinitely, as the paper copy remains the legal original
rationale: The trust protocol retains hard copies for a maximum of 28 days so the scan can be checked for completeness and legibility, with a second check by a different member of the team before cross shredding as confidential waste.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Receipt, Scrutiny and Management of Section Papers Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: December 2024, issue 04, review December 2027 (minor amendment June 2025)

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
question: Once section papers have been scanned onto SystmOne, which version does the trust treat as the original?
options: The paper copy filed in the Mental Health Act (MHA) office
The paper copy held in the patient's ward folder
The electronic version on SystmOne
Whichever copy the Responsible Clinician signed most recently
rationale: The trust protocol states that once section papers are uploaded to SystmOne the electronic version becomes the original, and hard copies are then securely destroyed.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Receipt, Scrutiny and Management of Section Papers Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: December 2024, issue 04, review December 2027 (minor amendment June 2025)

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
question: After the Mental Health Act (MHA) office has completed its administrative scrutiny, what happens next to the medical recommendations, and by when?
options: They are filed on the ward and reviewed at the next care planning meeting
They are e-mailed to Section 12 approved doctors in the trust for medical scrutiny, which must happen as soon as possible and not exceed 14 days from the start of detention
They are sent to the Responsible Clinician for countersignature within 72 hours
They are reviewed by the Mental Health Act Committee at its next quarterly meeting
rationale: The policy sets out a two-stage scrutiny: administrative scrutiny by the MHA office, then medical scrutiny by Section 12 approved doctors, which must take place as soon as possible and not exceeding 14 days since the start of the detention.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Receipt, Scrutiny and Management of Section Papers Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: December 2024, issue 04, review December 2027 (minor amendment June 2025)

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A patient is detained on the ward at 2pm on Monday.
question: Under the trust's Section 132 policy, by when must the patient be informed verbally of their rights, and by whom?
options: Within 24 hours of detention, by a member of the nursing team
Within 72 hours of detention, by the Responsible Clinician
Within 7 days, by the Mental Health Act (MHA) office
At the first ward round, by the Approved Mental Health Professional (AMHP)
rationale: The current version of the trust policy reduced the timescale to within 24 hours of detention in hospital, given verbally by a member of the nursing team and recorded in the Electronic Patient Record (EPR).
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Section 132: Patients' Rights Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
question: How often does the trust's Section 132 policy say it is good practice to remind a patient of their rights?
options: Monthly for all patients, whether detained or on a Community Treatment Order (CTO)
At least every 3 months for inpatients and every 6 months for patients on a Community Treatment Order (CTO)
At least every 6 months for inpatients and every 12 months for patients on a Community Treatment Order (CTO)
Only when the patient's legal status changes
rationale: The policy sets a reminder of rights at least every 3 months for inpatients and every 6 months for CTO patients, with a new questionnaire completed on SystmOne each time.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Section 132: Patients' Rights Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A rights questionnaire has not reached the Mental Health Act (MHA) office 30 hours after a patient was detained.
question: What does the trust's monitoring process say happens?
options: Nothing until the weekly audit report is produced
The Responsible Clinician is asked to complete the rights explanation instead
The Nurse in Charge of the ward is notified for follow-up, and a list of outstanding rights forms goes to the matron and senior nurses weekly
The section is treated as invalid until the questionnaire is received
rationale: The policy states that if a Section 132 notification is not received within 24 hours of detention the Nurse in Charge is notified for follow-up, with a weekly list of outstanding rights forms provided to the matron and senior nurses at the trust's inpatient units.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Section 132: Patients' Rights Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A newly detained patient is too distressed to take in anything you say about their rights.
question: What do the trust policies require you to do?
options: Leave the rights leaflet on their bed and treat the duty as discharged
Ask the Mental Health Act (MHA) office to send the information to the nearest relative instead
Wait until the Responsible Clinician can do it at the next ward round
Record on the Section 132 form and in the Electronic Patient Record (EPR) that they did not understand, and repeat the explanation until they fully understand
rationale: Both the Section 132 policy and the Receipt and Scrutiny policy require the lack of understanding to be recorded on the Section 132 form and in the EPR, with the explanation repeated by nursing staff until the patient fully understands.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Section 132: Patients' Rights Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
question: Who does the trust make responsible for reviewing and checking that the rights explanation is repeated until the patient understands?
options: The Mental Health Act (MHA) Administrator who processed the papers
The ward manager or their nominated deputy
The Responsible Clinician
The Independent Mental Health Advocate (IMHA)
rationale: The Receipt and Scrutiny policy places responsibility on the ward manager or nominated deputy to review and check that this process is repeated until the patient understands.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Receipt, Scrutiny and Management of Section Papers Policy and Procedure
sourceDate: December 2024, issue 04, review December 2027 (minor amendment June 2025)

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A detained patient speaks little English and you need to explain their rights.
question: Which interpreting arrangement does the trust's Section 132 policy point staff to?
options: Ask a family member to interpret
The Ministry of Justice interpreter service
The Mental Health Act (MHA) office keeps a rota of bilingual staff
Language Line Solutions, with details on the Focus intranet home page
rationale: The policy states the trust uses Language Line Solutions and that details are found on the Focus home page. The Ministry of Justice is only responsible for providing interpreters to attend a Mental Health Tribunal.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Section 132: Patients' Rights Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A patient tells you during the rights discussion that they are happy for their nearest relative to be told about the detention.
question: Who then writes to the nearest relative, and what triggers it?
options: The Mental Health Act (MHA) office writes once it has been notified that the rights questionnaire has been completed
The nurse who explained the rights writes the same day
The Responsible Clinician writes after the first ward round
No letter is sent unless the nearest relative asks for one
rationale: The policy states that when the MHA office has received notification that the rights questionnaire has been completed, and the patient does not object, it sends the nearest relative a letter enclosing the relevant patient information leaflet.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Section 132: Patients' Rights Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A patient in the community has been placed on a Community Treatment Order (CTO) and no Section 132A rights explanation has been recorded.
question: Under the trust's monitoring arrangements, who is notified if this is not recorded in the Electronic Patient Record (EPR) within the first month of the CTO commencing?
options: The Care Quality Commission (CQC)
The Service Line Manager
The Mental Health Act Committee
The patient's nearest relative
rationale: The Section 132 policy states that if a Section 132A explanation of rights is not recorded in the EPR within the first month of the CTO commencing, the Service Line Manager is notified for follow-up.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Section 132: Patients' Rights Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A detained patient asks to go to the shop with a visitor.
question: Under the trust's Section 17 policy, who is responsible for making sure a Section 17 leave form has been completed before the patient leaves hospital?
options: The Responsible Clinician, who must be on site
The Mental Health Act (MHA) office
The patient's named nurse, but only for escorted leave
The Nurse in Charge
rationale: The policy makes the Nurse in Charge responsible for ensuring a Section 17 form has been completed before the patient is allowed to leave hospital, and for keeping the form accessible to staff at all times.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Section 17 Leave, Mental Health Act 1983 Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: It is 11pm at the weekend and a detained patient needs leave authorising. The patient's usual Responsible Clinician is not available.
question: What does the trust's Section 17 policy say about who can grant the leave?
options: The Nurse in Charge may authorise it and inform the Responsible Clinician later
Any doctor on site may authorise it
Only the patient's Responsible Clinician may grant Section 17 leave, and out of hours the covering doctor will be the Consultant on call
The on-call manager may authorise it in the Responsible Clinician's absence
rationale: The policy is explicit that only the patient's Responsible Clinician may grant Section 17 leave and that the role may not be transferred or delegated, and that out of hours the covering doctor will be the Consultant on call.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Section 17 Leave, Mental Health Act 1983 Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A Responsible Clinician wants to grant a detained patient ten consecutive days of home leave.
question: What does the trust's Section 17 policy require?
options: Leave over seven days is not permitted under any circumstances

Section 17 leave should normally be no more than seven consecutive days, and before granting more the Responsible Clinician must consider whether the patient should be discharged onto a Community Treatment Order (CTO), with that discussion recorded in the Electronic Patient Record (EPR)
Leave over seven days needs written approval from the Mental Health Act (MHA) office
Leave over seven days needs approval from a Hospital Managers panel
rationale: The policy says Section 17 leave should normally be of short duration and not normally more than seven consecutive days, and that before exceeding this the Responsible Clinician is required to consider a CTO and record the discussion in the EPR.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Section 17 Leave, Mental Health Act 1983 Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A patient has authorised unescorted leave but you think they are more unwell today than they were yesterday.
question: What does the trust's Section 17 policy say about nursing staff withholding leave?
options: Nursing staff can never withhold leave once the Responsible Clinician has authorised it
Nursing staff may withhold leave if they consider the patient not well enough, but it is bad practice to withhold it for any reason other than a deterioration in the patient's mental state
Nursing staff may withhold leave for any operational reason, including staffing levels
Leave can only be withheld with the agreement of both the Nurse in Charge and the on-call manager
rationale: The policy requires nursing staff to assess the patient's clinical state before each instance of leave and permits them to withhold it if the patient is not well enough, while stating it is bad practice to withhold leave for any other reason.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Section 17 Leave, Mental Health Act 1983 Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A detained patient collapses and needs urgent transfer to the acute hospital. The Responsible Clinician cannot be reached immediately.
question: What does the trust's Section 17 policy say you should do?
options: Hold the patient on the ward until written Section 17 leave is in place
Send the patient and treat the transfer as a Section 19 transfer instead

Do not delay the transfer. Contact the Responsible Clinician for authorisation as soon as practicable, document any telephone authorisation in the clinical notes, and get a copy of the completed form to the acute trust as soon as practicable
Discharge the patient from their section so they can be treated informally at the acute hospital
rationale: The policy states that in an emergency the transfer must not be delayed, that the Responsible Clinician can authorise Section 17 leave over the telephone, that nursing staff must document the conversation in the clinical notes, and that the form must be completed at the earliest opportunity with a copy provided to the acute trust.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Section 17 Leave, Mental Health Act 1983 Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: The team is planning Section 17 leave for a detained patient to a residential care placement.
question: What does the trust's Section 17 policy say about funding?
options: Funding must be agreed by the Commissioning Manager for Mental Health and Learning Disability, it is the ward staff's responsibility to arrange this, and it cannot be agreed retrospectively
Funding is arranged by the local authority social worker after the leave has started
No funding agreement is needed while the patient remains detained
Funding is agreed by the Responsible Clinician as part of authorising the leave
rationale: The policy states that where Section 17 leave is to residential or nursing care, funding must be agreed by the Commissioning Manager for Mental Health and Learning Disability, that it is the responsibility of ward staff to arrange this, and that funding cannot be agreed retrospectively.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Section 17 Leave, Mental Health Act 1983 Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A detained patient is being considered for their first period of extended home leave.
question: What is the trust's default position on assessing the home environment?
options: A telephone call to the family is sufficient in the first instance
Repeated home visits are always required before any home leave is granted
The home environment is assessed only if the patient or family requests it

A face-to-face assessment in the patient's home environment is the default unless a documented risk assessment suggests otherwise, and a face-to-face assessment is needed on the first day at home if the patient is placed on extended leave
rationale: The policy sets the default as a face-to-face assessment in the home environment unless a documented risk assessment suggests otherwise, and requires a face-to-face assessment on the first day at home for patients placed on extended leave.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Section 17 Leave, Mental Health Act 1983 Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A detained patient does not come back from home leave and is refusing to return, and you know which address they are staying at.
question: What does the trust's Section 17 policy say about retaking them?
options: The police will always force entry on the ward's say-so with no further authority needed

It is the responsibility of the hospital to obtain a Section 135(2) warrant, applied for at the Magistrates Court by a member of trust staff, authorising a police officer to remove the patient using proportionate force
Only an Approved Mental Health Professional (AMHP) can retake the patient, and only from a public place
Nothing can be done until the patient's current period of detention expires
rationale: The policy states that where the patient is known to be staying at other premises and refusing to return, it is the hospital's responsibility to obtain a Section 135(2) warrant, with the application made to the Magistrates Court by a member of trust staff.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Section 17 Leave, Mental Health Act 1983 Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: You are recording a new period of Section 17 leave on SystmOne using the trust's Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).
question: After entering the expected departure and return dates and any notes, which two fields does the SOP tell you to complete before selecting the Section 17 template?
options: 'CTO considered' and 'Approved by'
'Risk assessed' and 'Escorted by'
'Nearest relative informed' and 'Section 132 given'
'Ward manager notified' and 'Care plan updated'
rationale: The trust's Section 17 SOP takes staff through Ward view, right clicking the patient, Administrative, Add Patient leave, then the expected departure and return dates, notes, the 'CTO considered' section and the 'Approved by' section, before selecting the Section 17 template.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Standard Operating Procedure: Section 17 (SystmOne)
sourceDate: Issue 01, no issue or review date shown on the document

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A patient admitted under Section 4 is examined by a second doctor within the 72 hour period and the section is converted to a Section 2.
question: What does the trust's Section 4 policy require of the ward's paperwork?
options: A fresh Form H3 is completed in full for the Section 2
Part 1 of Form H3 is completed on admission on Section 4, and Part 2 of Form H3 is completed when it converts to Section 2 within 72 hours
Form H1 is completed for the Section 4 and Form H3 for the Section 2
No further acceptance form is needed once the original Form H3 has been signed
rationale: The Section 4 policy states the Nurse in Charge completes Part 1 of Form H3 on admission under Section 4, and Part 2 of Form H3 if the section is converted to a Section 2 within the 72 hour period, with the papers then sent to the Mental Health Act Administrator without delay.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Section 4 Emergency Application for Detention Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A patient detained under Section 4 asks to go off the unit for an hour with a relative.
question: What does the trust's Section 4 policy say about Section 17 leave for this patient?
options: It can be granted for up to 2 hours by the Nurse in Charge
It can be granted by the Consultant on call only
Section 17 leave of absence is not applicable to a patient detained under Section 4
It can be granted but only once the second medical recommendation has been received
rationale: Both the Section 4 policy and the Section 17 policy state that Section 17 leave does not apply to patients detained under Section 4.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Section 4 Emergency Application for Detention Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
question: How often does the trust monitor the use of Section 4, and through which group?
options: Monthly, through the ward's clinical governance meeting
Annually, by the Care Quality Commission (CQC)
Weekly, by the Mental Health Act (MHA) office
Quarterly, by the Mental Health Act Committee
rationale: The Section 4 policy states that hospital managers and local authorities should monitor the use of Section 4 to ensure it is not misused, and that this is monitored quarterly by the Mental Health Act Committee.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Mental Health Act 1983 Section 4 Emergency Application for Detention Policy and Procedure

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: A ward clerk offers to scan a set of section papers straight onto the patient's SystmOne record to save time.
question: What does the trust's Mental Health Act (MHA) Documents Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) say?
options: Any registered nurse may upload section papers to SystmOne
The ward clerk may upload them if the Nurse in Charge countersigns
Only staff within the MHA office can record MHA information and documentation onto SystmOne
The Responsible Clinician uploads them as part of the admission review
rationale: The SOP is explicit that only staff within the MHA office can record MHA information and documentation onto SystmOne, and that all original section papers must be sent on receipt to the appropriate MHA office for scrutiny, processing and uploading.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Standard Operating Procedure: MHA Documents (SystmOne)
sourceDate: Issue 01, no issue or review date shown on the document

category: Trust Policy - Mental Health Act (local process)
scenario: You need to check a patient's current legal status and the key dates connected to their section before handover.
question: Where does the trust's Mental Health Act (MHA) Documents Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) tell you to look on SystmOne?
options: The Alerts panel on the patient's home screen
The Ward view summary bar, which lists every patient's section
The scanned documents folder in the patient's communications record
The MHA node in the clinical tree within the patient record, using the Show Previous Sections tick box for historical sections
rationale: The SOP directs staff to the MHA node in the clinical tree to see current sections, with a view dropdown to filter sections recorded here or elsewhere, and a Show Previous Sections tick box for historical sections.
source: Derbyshire Healthcare - Standard Operating Procedure: MHA Documents (SystmOne)
sourceDate: Issue 01, no issue or review date shown on the document
